en: The lands which the German Empire has lost in the course of several centuries make up a long, sad list.

The teachers of constitutional law, partly because the laws of the constitution and of the organization of state power have altogether come to nothing [are] and give little or nothing to treat of, must hold to the description of the signs that have become empty and meaningless as insignia of what was, and of the claims, partly these claims carry with them precisely that consoling emotion with which an impoverished nobleman preserves the last remains of his vanished ancestors, - a consolation that has the advantage of remaining secure and undisturbed.

As little as these paintings are able to make objections to the present owners of their knightly estates, so little have the constitutional claims of the German Empire ever caused a minister the anxiety of expecting a contradiction from him; both, the nobleman and the teacher of constitutional law, can calmly abandon themselves to their innocent and harmless delights.
zh: 德意志帝国在几百年间陆续失去的那些地方，构成了一份长长的、令人悲伤的清单。
国家法教师们的处境是这样：一方面，宪法和国家权力组织的各项法律整个已经化为乌有[了]，可讲的东西很少甚至没有，他们便只好去描述那些已经变得空洞而无意义的标记、把它们当作过去之物的徽章，去描述那些要求；另一方面，这些要求本身就带着那种令人慰藉的感动，就像一个破了产的贵族守着先人消逝后留下的最后一点遗物时所怀的那种感动，——这种慰藉有一个好处，就是安稳而不受打扰。
这些画像并不能对骑士庄园如今的主人提出什么异议，同样，德意志帝国那些国家法上的要求，也从来没有让哪位大臣担心过会遭到他的反对；贵族和国家法教师这两个人，尽可以安安静静地沉溺于他们那无辜而无害的消遣。

en: If the teachers of constitutional law still amuse themselves by expounding the claims of the Holy Roman-German Empire to Hungary, Poland, Prussia, Naples, etc., then, as to the political unimportance of such rights, it is also to be remarked that they concern not so much the German Empire as such, but rather the Roman imperial dignity, the head of Christendom and the lord of the world, and [that] the Roman Emperor and King in Germany, as his title declared it, were [in essence] separate.

The German Empire could have neither the interest, nor the will, nor later the strength to assert that which could be counted as belonging to the Emperor's overlordship, and such an unnatural union of lands, which their geographical position separated just as much as the individuality of the peoples, all the less since it itself neither would nor could keep those lands that were integral parts of it.
zh: 如果国家法教师们至今还以阐述神圣罗马帝国对匈牙利、波兰、普鲁士、那不勒斯等等的权利为乐，那么，关于这类权利在政治上的无足轻重，也还要指出：它们涉及的与其说是德意志帝国本身，不如说是罗马皇帝的尊位，即基督教世界的首领和世界之主；而罗马皇帝和在日耳曼的国王，正如他的头衔所表明的，[在本质上]是彼此分开的。
德意志帝国既没有兴趣，也没有意志，后来更没有力量去坚持那些可以算作皇帝最高统治权的东西，去坚持这样一种不自然的、由若干地方拼成的结合——这些地方既被它们的地理位置分隔，也被各族的个体性分隔；更何况，它连那些本来就是它组成部分的地方，也既不愿意又不能够保住。

en: Of the connection of the Lombard kingdom, traces have still been preserved down to the latest times, but one cannot regard it as an essential part of the proper German kingdom, all the less since it was itself a kingdom of its own, and the German imperial estatehood, which belonged to some of its states, had long since lost its force.
zh: 与伦巴德王国的结合，直到最晚近的时代还留有痕迹，但不能把它看作本来意义上的德意志王国的一个本质部分，更何况它本身就是一个自己的王国，而它的某些邦所拥有的德意志帝国等级资格，早已失去了效力。

en: But with regard to the lands that essentially belonged to the German Empire and possessed and exercised imperial estatehood, almost every war of the Empire has ended with the loss of some of them.
zh: 但就那些本质上属于德意志帝国、并拥有和行使帝国等级资格的地方来说，帝国几乎每一场战争都以失去其中某几处而告终。

en: This loss really comprehends in itself two kinds: namely, besides the actual subjugation of German lands under foreign overlordship and their complete tearing loose from all rights and duties toward the Empire, it must be regarded as a loss for the state that so many lands indeed remained in every hitherto legal and apparent relation toward Emperor and Empire, but received princes who, in that they became or were members of the Empire, are at the same time monarchs of independent states.

It is this circumstance that is seemingly no loss, but seemingly left everything as of old, yet has undermined the coherence of the state in its foundation pillars, because these lands thereby became independent of the state power.
zh: 这种损失实际上包含两类：一类是德意志的地方真正屈服于外国的最高统治，并被彻底割断对帝国的一切权利和义务；另一类也必须看作国家的损失，就是有那么多地方虽然在迄今一切法律上和表面上的关系上都留在皇帝和帝国这边，却得到了这样的君主——他们成为或本来就是帝国成员，同时又是独立国家的君主。
正是这种情况表面上不是损失，表面上让一切照旧，却从根基上挖空了国家的联结，因为这些地方由此不再受国家权力的支配。

en: Without going back to older times, we give only a brief survey of how, from the Peace of Westphalia onward, the powerlessness of Germany and its necessary fate in relation to foreign powers has expressed itself; it can of course be a question only of its loss of lands in the peace settlements, for the damage through war is immeasurable for every account.
zh: 不必回到更早的时代，我们只简要地看一看：从《威斯特伐利亚和约》起，德意志的软弱无力以及它在同外国列强的关系中那种必然的命运是怎样表现出来的；当然，这里只能谈它在各次和约中的失地，因为战争造成的损失是任何统计都无法衡量的。

en: In the Peace of Westphalia there was lost not only all connection of the United Netherlands with the German Empire, but also that of Switzerland, whose independence had long since taken place in practice, but was now formally recognized, - a loss not of possession, but of claims, which in itself is not significant, but is important for the German Empire, which has often shown that chimeras of claims and rights that lack all reality are held by it higher than an actual possession. - Thus Germany too now formally ceded to France the bishoprics of Metz, Toul and Verdun, which it had already lost a century before.
But a real loss for the Empire was the cession of the landgraviate of Alsace, namely insofar as Austria had possessed it, and of the imperial city of Bisanz [Besançon] to Spain.
zh: 在《威斯特伐利亚和约》里失去的，不仅是联合尼德兰同德意志帝国的一切联系，还有瑞士同帝国的联系——瑞士的独立早已在实际中成立，这时只是得到正式承认罢了，——这是一种并非丧失占有、而是丧失要求的损失，它本身并不重大，对德意志帝国却很重要，因为这个帝国常常表明，那些毫无实在性的要求和权利的幻影，在它看来比现实的占有还要高。 ——同样，德意志这时也正式向法国让出了梅斯、图勒和凡尔登这三个主教区，而它在此前整整一个世纪就已经失去了它们。
但对帝国来说现实的损失，是把阿尔萨斯领地伯爵领——即奥地利曾经占有的那部分——以及帝国城市比桑[贝桑松]割让给了西班牙。

en: These lands stepped out of all connection with Germany, but more than these indeed remained in their legal and theoretical dependence, yet that their princes were at the same time foreign monarchs laid the ground for their real separation in practice.
To Sweden, namely, came Hither Pomerania and a part of Further Pomerania, the archbishopric of Bremen and the bishopric of Verden and the city of Wismar.
To the Margrave of Brandenburg, Duke and afterwards King of Prussia, came the archbishopric of Magdeburg, the bishopric of Halberstadt, Kammin and Minden.
zh: 这些地方退出了同德意志的一切联系；但除它们之外还有更多地方，虽然仍旧处在法律上和理论上的依附之中，可它们的君主同时又是外国的君主，这就为它们在实际上真正分离打下了基础。
归瑞典的，是前波美拉尼亚和后波美拉尼亚的一部分、不来梅大主教区、费尔登主教区以及维斯马城。
归勃兰登堡藩侯、普鲁士公爵和后来的普鲁士国王的，是马格德堡大主教区，以及哈尔伯施塔特、卡明和明登这几个主教区。

en: Even if the Prince of Brandenburg had not at the same time been a sovereign, this diminution of the number of German estates and their fusion into one mass would have produced only a little different effect, namely to form a state power that could henceforth refuse the German state power subordination and offer it resistance, which the very same power, distributed among several, could not.
zh: 即使勃兰登堡的君主不同时是一位主权者，德意志各等级数目的这种减少和它们融合成一团，也只会产生一种差别不大的效果，就是形成一个国家权力，它从此能够拒绝服从德意志的国家权力，并对它进行抵抗；而同一个权力要是分散在若干人手里，就做不到这一点。

en: Besides this diminution that has been cited, several more particular estates also came to an end, Schwerin, Ratzeburg, etc.
zh: 除了上面提到的这种减少之外，还有好几个单独的等级也消亡了，什未林、拉策堡等等。

en: Just as destructive for the German state was the circumstance that the German Empire transferred to foreign powers - after these had, both by force and when called, mixed themselves into Germany's affairs and devastated it from one end to the other and more or less dictated the peace - in this peace the guarantee over its constitution and internal relations, and thereby acknowledged its incapacity to preserve itself as a state and its constitution, as it surrendered its internal affairs to the interest of foreigners.
zh: 对德意志国家同样起破坏作用的，是这样一种情况：外国列强无论凭武力还是受邀请，都插手了德意志的事务，把它从一头蹂躏到另一头，并或多或少地主宰了和约，而德意志帝国在这次和约中把对自己宪法和内部关系的保证交给了它们，从而承认自己没有能力把自己作为国家和把自己的宪法维持下去，也就等于把自己的内部事务交到外国人的利益手里。

en: Other internal weakenings [were] the granting of privileges of appeal to several lands, in part also the permission of the choice of the imperial court before which the defendant wished to be sued, since the defendant can delay the course of law all the more by delaying the choice; still more than all this the establishment of the right that not only in religious matters, and indeed also in those that concern entirely the external religious condition, the purely worldly part of it, but also in other objects that concern the whole Empire, the majority of votes at the imperial diet should not be binding, - that the German Empire should no longer be allowed to redeem its sovereign rights pledged to imperial cities, etc.
zh: 另一些内部的削弱[是]：给好几个地方颁发上诉特权，在某种程度上还允许由被告挑选审理他的帝国法院，因为被告只要拖延这个挑选，就能把诉讼拖得更久；比这一切更严重的是这样一条规定的确立：不仅在宗教事务上——而且包括那些完全涉及宗教外部状况、即其纯世俗部分的宗教事务——而且在其他涉及整个帝国的对象上，帝国议会中多数票都不应有约束力，——还有，德意志帝国不得再赎回它抵押给帝国城市的那些主权权利，等等。

en: In the next peace settlement, namely the Nijmegen one, which came about without an imperial deputation but was ratified by the Empire - and thereby also its clause that on the Empire's part no contradiction against it should be accepted -, the Empire's sovereignty over the county of Burgundy was given up, and some stretches of land in northern Germany changed their lords, and in the southern [changed] France's rights of garrison in German fortresses.
zh: 在下一次和约、即《奈梅亨和约》中——这次和约没有帝国代表团参与便缔结了，却由帝国批准，因而也就批准了其中那条：帝国方面不得对它提出任何异议——，帝国对勃艮第伯国的最高权被放弃了，德意志北部有几片土地换了主人，南部则［改变了］法国在德意志各要塞的驻军权。

en: But besides its loss in peace settlements, the German Empire presents phenomena entirely its own, which hardly occurred with other states: in the deepest peace, namely after the Peace of Nijmegen, ten imperial cities of Alsace and other regions were lost to France.
zh: 但除了在和约中的损失之外，德意志帝国还呈现出一些完全属于它自己的现象，这类现象在别的国家不大容易出现：在最深沉的和平之中，也就是在《奈梅亨和约》之后，阿尔萨斯的十座帝国城市和其他一些地方丢给了法国。

en: The Peace of Ryswick was concluded in the presence of an imperial deputation in such a way that the latter [was] not admitted to the conferences with the foreign envoys, but received news at the discretion of the imperial [envoy] and was addressed for its assent.

This peace settlement confirmed the French taking of possession of those lands, acquired for the Empire in return one imperial fortress, Kehl, but contained the famous clause concerning the religious condition in the conquered lands returned by France, which gave the Protestant estates so much to do and helped bring so much misfortune over the Palatinate.
zh: 《赖斯韦克和约》是在一个帝国代表团在场的情况下这样缔结的：代表团[不被]允许参加同外国使节的会谈，而是听凭皇帝[使节]的意思得到消息，并被请求表示赞同。
这次和约确认了法国对那些地方的占有，反过来为帝国换来一座帝国要塞——凯尔，但其中含有那条著名的、关于法国归还的被征服地区宗教状况的条款，这条条款给新教各等级添了那么多事，也帮着给普法尔茨带来了那么多灾祸。

en: In the Baden peace negotiations no imperial deputation took part, and the peace settlement itself also brought about no immediate change for the German Empire; Austria got Breisach and Freiburg back.
zh: 巴登和谈没有帝国代表团参加，和约本身也没有给德意志帝国带来直接的变化；奥地利收回了布赖萨赫和弗赖堡。

en: This is actually the last peace that the German Empire has concluded.153) If, then, according to a tabular survey of imperial history from the Peace of Baden to the Seven Years' imperial war, one finds neither declarations of war nor peace settlements, one would have to believe that Germany enjoyed the deepest peace throughout this long period, while its soil was as much as ever the scene of battles and devastations.
zh: 这其实是德意志帝国缔结的最后一次和约。153) 所以，如果按照一份从《巴登和约》到七年帝国战争的帝国史表格来看，既找不到宣战，也找不到和约，那人们就不得不相信，德意志在这段漫长的时期里享受着最深沉的和平，而它的土地却一如既往地是战场和遭蹂躏的地方。

en: The peace treaties which Sweden concluded after the death of Charles XII with Hanover, Prussia, Denmark and Russia took from it not only the place among the powers of Europe which its brave king had forced for it, but it also lost its power in Germany; yet through the latter circumstance the German state power gained nothing, for the lands which Sweden lost came to German princes, who stepped into its place as regards the fearsomeness for Germany's unity.
zh: 瑞典在卡尔十二世死后同汉诺威、普鲁士、丹麦和俄国缔结的各项和约，不仅夺走了它的勇敢国王为它逼出来的那个在欧洲列强中的位置，而且它还失去了它在德意志的势力；但通过后一情况，德意志的国家权力什么也没有得到，因为瑞典所失去的那些地方落到了德意志的诸侯手里，他们就取代了它对德意志统一所具有的那种可怕地位。

en: In the Peace of Vienna Germany lost nothing but the relation of Lorraine, which was anyway slight; it did not come to a ratification of this peace by the Empire.
zh: 在维也纳和约中，德意志除了洛林的那种关系以外什么也没有失去，而那种关系本来就微不足道；这次和约没有到由帝国批准这一步。

en: In the Austrian War of Succession Germany was the theatre of protracted devastations.
Its greatest princes were entangled in it; the armies of foreign monarchs fought on its soil, and yet the German Empire was in the deepest peace.
The power that had stepped into Sweden's place, Prussia, enlarged itself in this war.
zh: 在奥地利王位继承战争中，德意志是长年累月的蹂躏的舞台。
它最大的几位诸侯都被卷了进去；外国君主的军队在它的土地上打仗，而德意志帝国却处在最深的和平之中。
取代了瑞典位置的那个势力，即普鲁士，在这场战争中壮大了自己。

en: Far more devastating still, especially for northern Germany, was the Seven Years' War.

The German Empire did indeed also wage war this time, namely a war of execution against eight, but its enemies did not even do it the honour of acknowledging that it was waging war, nor of concluding peace with it.
zh: 还要更具毁灭性的，尤其对北德意志来说，是七年战争。
德意志帝国这次固然也打了仗，而且是一场对八方的执行战争，但它的敌人甚至不肯给它这份面子，既不肯承认它在打仗，也不肯同它缔结和约。

en: The Peace of Lunéville has finally not only taken from Germany many rights of overlordship in Italy, but torn away from it the whole left bank of the Rhine and already in itself diminished the number of its princes and laid a ground which will diminish the number of its estates still by many and make the individual parts all the more fearsome for the whole and for the smaller estates.
zh: 吕内维尔和约最终不仅从德意志手里拿走了它在意大利的许多宗主权，而且夺走了整条莱茵河左岸，并且光凭它自己就已经减少了它的诸侯数目，还奠定了一个根据，这根据将把它的等级数目再减少许多，并使各个单独的部分对整体和对较小的等级变得更加可怕。

en: A land whose one half in war either brawls about among itself or gives up the common defence and by neutrality surrenders the other half to the enemy must be mangled in war and chopped to pieces in peace, because the strength of a land consists neither in the number of its inhabitants and warriors, nor in its fertility, nor in its size, but solely in the manner in which, through rational connection of the parts into one state power, all this can be used for the great end of the common defence.
zh: 一个国家，它的一半在战争中要么自己内部互相厮打，要么放弃共同的防卫，靠中立把另一半交给敌人，这样的国家在战争里必被撕碎，在和平里必被切成碎块，因为一个国家的力量既不在于它的居民和战士的数量，也不在于它的肥沃，也不在于它的广大，而仅仅在于这种方式：通过把各部分理性地联结成一种国家权力，这一切都能被用于共同防卫这个伟大目的。

en: If now Germany in its war power and money power forms no state power within itself and therefore must be regarded not as a state but as a multitude of independent states, of which the larger ones also act externally in an independent way, while the smaller ones must follow some great procession or other and the associations which now and then come about under the name of the German Empire for some particular purpose are always concluded partially and according to the allies' own pleasure, then these associations lack all the advantage which the coalitions of other powers can have; for in such coalitions, even if they are of no long duration and even while they last do not in certain cases, as in wars, work with the success and emphasis that would obtain if the very same power stood entirely under one government, the measures and means most serviceable to that which is the purpose of the allies are taken up with understanding, and accordingly everything is arranged with a view to that purpose.

But the coalitions of the German estates are bound by such formalities, restrictions and endless considerations as they have created for themselves to this end, that thereby every effect of the coalition is paralysed, and it has already been made impossible in advance to attain that which it has proposed to itself.
zh: 如果说德意志在它的战争力量和金钱力量上并没有在自己内部形成一种国家权力，因此不能被视为一个国家，而只能被视为一大堆独立的国家——其中较大的那些在对外上也是独立行动的，较小的那些则不得不跟随某个大国的行进，而偶尔为了某个特定目的在德意志帝国这个名义下凑成的各种联合，总是局部的，并且是按照结盟者自己的心意缔结的——那么这些联合就缺少其他列强的同盟所能具有的一切好处；因为在这样的同盟里，即使它们不能长久维持，甚至就在它们存在期间，在某些场合，比如在战争里，也不能像同一种势力完全处于一个政府之下时那样取得成效和力度，人们还是会用知性采取对结盟者的目的最有用处的措施和手段，并据此把一切都朝着那个目的安排。
但德意志各等级的联合却被它们为此给自己造出来的那些形式、限制和无穷的顾虑束缚住了，以致联合的一切作用都被麻痹，而且要想达到它给自己定下的那个目标，事先就已经成为不可能了。

en: What the German Empire does as such is never an act of the whole, but of an association having a greater or lesser extent.

But the means of attaining that which the participants in it arrange are not taken for this purpose; rather the first and the only concern is that the relations of the confederates be held to which determine their being separate and their not being associated.
zh: 德意志帝国作为这样的东西所做的事，从来都不是整体的一种行动，而是一个范围或大或小的联合的行动。
但用来达到参与这一联合者所安排的事情的那些手段，却不是为这个目的而采取的，相反，首要的并且唯一的操心是：要守住结盟者之间的那些关系，而这些关系恰恰规定着他们的彼此分离以及他们并没有联合起来。

en: Such associations are like a heap of round stones that come together into a pyramid, but because they are absolutely round and are to remain so without fitting themselves together, as soon as the pyramid begins to move toward the purpose for which it has formed itself, it rolls apart, or at least can offer no resistance.

Through such an arrangement these states lack not only the infinite advantage that a state union has, but also the advantage of independence, of being able to join with others for particular common purposes: for for this case they have laid fetters upon themselves, whereby every union comes to nothing or is nothing already in its beginning.
zh: 这样的联合就像一堆圆石头，它们凑成一座金字塔，但正因为它们是绝对圆的，而且应当不彼此贴合地保持下去，所以一旦金字塔开始朝着它形成时所指向的那个目的动起来，它就滚散了，或者至少不能作出任何抵抗。
通过这样一种安排，这些国家不仅缺少国家联合所具有的那种无限的好处，而且缺少独立性的好处，即能够为了某些共同的特定目的同别的国家结合起来：因为为了这种情形，它们已经给自己套上了枷锁，任何联合都由此化为乌有，或者一开始就什么也不是。

en: Although in this way the German estates have abolished their union and shut themselves off from the possibility of joining together with understanding according to need and necessity for passing, momentary purposes, the demand is nevertheless present that Germany should be a state.

The contradiction is set up, so to determine the relations of the estates that no state is possible or actual, and yet Germany is to count absolutely as a state, it wants to regard itself absolutely as one body.

This spirit has for centuries thrown Germany between its will to make a state impossible and the will to be a state, into a series of inconsistencies, and made it unhappy between the estates' jealousy of every kind of subjection to the whole and the impossibility of subsisting without this subjection.
zh: 尽管德意志各等级以这种方式扬弃了它们的联合，并且对自己堵死了这种可能性：为了过渡性的、一时的目的，按需要和急难用知性结合起来，但那个要求仍然存在，即德意志应当是一个国家。
这里立起了矛盾：把各等级的关系规定得既不可能有国家也不会有现实的国家，可德意志又应当绝对地被当作一个国家，它绝对地想要把自己看作一个身体。
这种精神几个世纪以来把德意志抛在它的两种意志之间——一种是让国家成为不可能的意志，一种是要成为一个国家的意志——抛进一连串的不一致之中，并使它不幸地夹在各等级对每一种服从整体的方式的猜忌和没有这种服从就无法存续之间。

en: The solution of the problem, how it could be possible that Germany be no state and yet be a state, comes out very easily in this way, that it is a state in thoughts and no state in actuality, that formality and reality separate, the empty formality belongs to the state, but the reality to the non-being of the state.
zh: 这个问题——德意志怎么可能既不是国家又是国家——的解答很轻易地就得出来了：它在思想里是国家，在现实性里不是国家，形式与实在分离开来，空洞的形式归于国家，而实在则归于国家的非存在。

en: The system of the thought-state is the organisation of a legal constitution which in that which belongs to the essence of a state has no force.

The obligations of each estate toward emperor and Empire, toward the supreme government, which consists in the head in connection with the estates, are determined most precisely by an infinity of solemn and fundamental-legal acts.

These duties and rights make up a system of laws according to which the constitutional relation of each estate and the binding character of its contribution is most precisely fixed, and only according to these legal determinations is the contribution of each individual estate to be made for the common good.

But the nature of this legality consists in this, that the constitutional relation and its obligations are not determined according to general, proper laws, but, after the manner of civil rights, the relation of each estate to the whole is something particular in the form of a property.
Hereby the nature of the state power is essentially affected.
zh: 思想国家的体系是一种法权宪制的组织，而这种组织在属于一个国家之本质的事情上没有任何力量。
每个等级对皇帝和帝国、对最高政府的义务——这个政府存在于元首同各等级的结合之中——都由无穷无尽的庄严的、根本法的行为极其精确地规定下来。
这些义务和权利构成一个法律体系，按照这个体系，每个等级的国家法关系以及它应作贡献的约束力都被极其精确地确定下来，并且只有按照这些法律上的规定，各个单独等级为公共事务所作的贡献才应当发生。
但这种合法性的本性却在于：国家法关系及其义务并不是按照普遍的、真正的法律来确定的，而是像市民权利那样，每个等级对整体的关系是以一种所有权的形式出现的某种特殊东西。
由此，国家权力的本性就受到了本质性的影响。

en: An act that flows from the state power is a general one, and through its true universality it at the same time contains in itself the rule of its application.
That which it concerns is a universal, self-same thing.

The act of the state power brings a free and general determinacy into it, and its execution is at the same time its application, just as its application, because in that to which it applies itself there is nothing distinguishable, must be determined in the act itself and no brittle and unequal material resists its application.
zh: 从国家权力中流出的一项行为是普遍的行为，而通过它真正的普遍性，它同时把自身运用的规则包含在自身之内。
它所涉及的东西是一个普遍的、自身等同的东西。
国家权力的行为带进来一种自由的、普遍的规定性，而它的执行同时就是它的运用，正如它的运用——因为在它所要运用的东西上没有任何可区分的东西——必须在行为自身中得到规定，并没有任何生硬而不齐的材料抵抗它的运用。

en: When the act issues from the state power, that the hundredth man of a determinate age shall present himself as a soldier, or that a certain percentage of property or a determinate levy from every hide of land shall be paid, then that about which the decree is made is quite in general men of determinate age, property or land, and there is no difference among men and men, property [and property], land and land; the determinateness that comes into the self-same surface can be posited purely by the state power.

The hundredth man, the fifth percent, etc., are these quite general determinatenesses, which require no particular application in order to be entered into the self-same material; for no lines are described that would first have to be erased, or to which the determinate ones would have to be adjusted — as on a tree trunk the straight line according to which it is to be hewn.
zh: 当国家权力发出这样一项行为，即规定某一年龄的第一百个男子要作为士兵去报到，或者规定要缴纳财产的一定百分比、或者从每一胡弗土地上缴纳一定数额的赋税，那么被下令规定的东西，完全一般地就是某一年龄、财产或土地的人，而人与人、财产〔与财产〕、土地与土地之间没有任何区别；进入那块自身相等的平面的规定性，可以纯粹由国家权力来设定。
第一百个人、百分之五等等，就是这些完全一般的规定性，要把它们写进那自身相等的材料，并不需要任何特别的应用；因为这里并没有画出什么线条，需要先擦掉、或者要让那些确定的线条与之相合——就像在树干上画出那条要照它来砍削的直线一样。

en: But if that to which the law is to apply itself is manifoldly determined for this law itself, then the law cannot completely contain the rule of application within itself; on the contrary, for each particular part of the material there is a proper application, and between the law and its execution there steps the proper act of application, which belongs to the judicial power.
zh: 但如果法律所要适用的东西，对这条法律本身来说是具有多种规定性的，那么法律就不能把应用的规则完整地包含在自身之内；恰恰相反，对材料的每一个特殊部分来说都有一种自己的应用，而在法律和它的执行之间，插进了应用本身的行为，这一行为属于司法权力。

en: An imperial law can therefore not, as for an unwritten tablet, give the general rule of the lines and divisions that are to be made in it, nor execute the actual arrangement according to such one and the same rule; rather, the material for which it is made confronts an imperial law in its own, already previously given determinatenesses, and before its execution the possibility is first to be adjusted, how the particular line and shape that each part bears could fit with the one prescribed by the law, or how much obligation the general law has for each.

This, in case contradictions arise, a judicial power has to adjust; and with regard to this adjustment it in fact turns out that the adjustment is indeed to take place, but that, first, it is so organized that little can be adjusted by it; secondly, that what it has adjusted in theory is again not realized, remains an adjustment in thought; and finally that the whole business of adjustment is thereby made only somewhat less than impossible, in that the particular determinateness that the material has stands toward a general law in the relation of a straight line to a circular arc, so that from the outset there [exists] an incompatibility of this determinateness of the general material of the state power with a law of the same.

In this way the thought-state and the system of state right and of state laws are the straight line; but that in which the thought-state is to realize itself has the shape of a circular line, and one knows that the two lines are incommensurable; and this circular shape does not de facto make itself into this incompatibility with the straight line either; it does not bear the form of force, injustice and arbitrariness, but that it is this incommensurable line is likewise raised into the form of right: it acts rightfully in that it does not agree with state right, [and] lawfully in that it does not agree with state laws.
zh: 因此，一部帝国法律不能像面对一块还没写过的石板那样，给出要在上面划出的线条和分区的普遍规则，也不能按照这样一条唯一相同的规则去实施现实的安排；相反，一部帝国法律所为之而制定的材料，是以它自己那些早已给定的规定性来与这部法律相对的，而在实施之前，先要调处的是这样一种可能性：每一部分所带的特殊线条和形状，怎样才能与法律所规定的合上，或者说，这条普遍的法律对每一个部分究竟有多大的约束力。

一旦出现矛盾，这就要由司法权力来调处；而就这种调处而言，实际得出的结果是：调处固然应当进行，但第一，它的组织方式使得它能调处出来的东西很少；第二，它在理论上调处出来的东西又不会被实现，始终只是思想中的一种调处；最后，调处的这整个工作之所以只比不可能稍微好一点，是因为材料所具有的那种特殊规定性，对一条普遍的法律来说，处在一根直线对一段圆弧的关系里，所以，国家权力的普遍材料的这种规定性与它的一条法律之间，事先就已经〔存在〕不相容。
这样一来，思想国家以及国家法和国家法律的体系，就是那条直线；而思想国家要在其中实现自身的东西，却具有一条圆线的形状，而人们知道，这两条线是不可通约的；这种圆的形状事实上也不使自己成为与直线的那种不相容；它并不带有暴力、不法和任意的形式，相反，它是这样一条不可通约的线，这一点同样被提升到了法的形式之中：它行事合乎权利，因为它与国家法不相容，〔又〕合乎法律，因为它与国家法律不相容。

en: So that therefore the problem, how Germany is a state and at the same time no state, may be solved, it must, insofar as it would be a state, exist merely as thought-state, while the non-being of the state has the reality.

Now in order that the thought-state be for itself, the judicial power — which would want to sublate the contradiction and to apply that which is only thought to actuality, thus to realize it and to make actuality conform to it — must be so constituted that its application too remains only a thought, and thus the general ordinances through which the land would be a state are paralyzed in their transition into reality, and this transition itself is indeed itself posited and ordained — for the ordinances have no sense at all if they do not have the purpose of being executed — but the act of the transition too would again be made into a thought-thing.
zh: 因此，要使德国既是一个国家、同时又不是一个国家这个问题得到解决，那么，就它是一个国家而言，它必须仅仅作为思想国家而存在，而国家的非存在却拥有实在性。
而为了使思想国家自为地存在，司法权力——它想扬弃矛盾，想把仅仅是思想的东西应用到现实性上，从而把它实现出来、使现实性合乎它——就必须是这样一种情况：它的应用也仍然只是一个思想，于是，那些本来会使这片土地成为一个国家的普遍规章，在向实在性过渡时就被麻痹了，而这种过渡本身虽然也被设定、被安排——因为这些规章倘若没有被执行的目的，就毫无意义——，但过渡的行为却又被弄成了一个思想物。

en: The paralysis of this transition can happen at every one of its stages.
A general ordinance is made, it is to be executed, and in case of refusal judicial proceedings are to be taken.

If the refusal that what is due be rendered is not made judicial, then the execution remains lying there in itself; if it is made judicial, then the judgment can be prevented; if it comes about, then it is not complied with.
But this thought-thing of a resolution is to be executed and a punishment is to be imposed, so the order is given for the enforcement that is to be compelled.
This order is again not executed, so a resolution must follow against those who do not execute, to compel them to execute.
This again is not complied with, so it must be decreed that the punishment be carried out on those who do not carry it out on him who does not carry it out, and so on.
This is the dry story of how one stage after another, which a law is to set to work, is made into a thought-thing.
zh: 这种过渡的麻痹可以发生在它的每一个阶段上。
作出一项普遍的规章，它应当被执行，而在有人拒绝时应当走司法程序。
如果对应当履行的东西的拒绝不被提交司法处理，那么执行就搁在那里、自在不动；如果被提交司法处理，那么判决可以被阻止；判决如果作成了，又不会得到遵从。
但这个决议这件思想物却应当被执行、应当处以刑罚，于是就要为这种须以强制取得的执行发出命令。
这道命令又没有被执行，于是就必须作出一项针对那些不执行者的决议，迫使他们去执行。
这一决议又得不到遵从，于是就必须下令：对那些不肯向那个不执行刑罚的人执行刑罚的人，要执行刑罚，如此等等。
这就是那个干巴巴的故事：一条法律本来要用以实现自身的那些阶段，是怎样一个接一个地被弄成思想物的。

en: If therefore it is to be adjusted through the judicial power how the general imperial obligations are to be brought into comparison with the particular rights of individuals, and a contradiction of these really becomes judicial, then it depends on the organization that the court has in its judging business even without relation to execution, whether the judging is not already made difficult for it and — since the judgment, if it is not executed, is in itself a mere thought — whether the arrangement is not such that it does not even come to this thought, but that this thought too remains a mere thought-thing.
zh: 所以，如果要通过司法权力来调处普遍的帝国义务怎样与个人的特殊权利相比较，而它们之间的矛盾现实地进入了司法程序，那么就取决于法院在它的审判事务中、甚至在还不涉及执行时所具有的那种组织方式：审判是不是已经变得困难了——因为判决如果不被执行，自在的只是一个单纯的思想——，以及这种安排是不是根本连这个思想都到不了，而是连这个思想也停留为一个单纯的思想物。

en: In relation to the mere pronouncing of judgment, the organization of the judicial power is already so constituted that its essential side, which is at issue here, that of making the general ordinances of the state as state valid against individuals, suffers the greatest hindrances.
In the imperial judicial power, civil jurisdiction and that state-right jurisdiction are mixed together.
State right and private right are subject to the same courts.
The imperial courts are the supreme courts of appeal for civil lawsuits and for state rights.

The extent of their judicial power over the latter, however limited it otherwise is, in that the most important things of this kind belong before the imperial diet, and much that belongs here is also decided by arbitration instances, suffers infinite difficulties even for the mere pronouncing of judgment and is made dependent on a multitude of contingencies which become necessities for its ineffectiveness.
zh: 单就审判来说，司法权力的组织就已经是这样一种情况：它那个这里所谈到的本质方面，即把国家作为国家的普遍规章对个人主张出来，遭受着最大的阻碍。
在帝国的司法权力中，民事司法和那种国家法司法是混在一起的。
国家法和私法服从于同样的法院。
帝国法院是审理民事法律纠纷和国家法权利的最高上诉法院。
它们对后一类事情的司法权力的范围，尽管本来就很有限——因为这类事情中最重要的东西要归帝国议会，而且有许多属于这里的事情是由仲裁法庭裁定的——，却单是就审判而言也遭受着无穷的困难，并且被弄成依赖一大堆偶然情况，而这些偶然情况对它的不起作用来说就变成了必然。

en: The combination of a civil and a state-right jurisdiction has in general already the effect of so enlarging the mass of business of the existing imperial courts that they are unable to dispatch it.
It is acknowledged by Emperor and Empire and by the imperial chamber court that the imperial chamber court is even less equal to the mass of its business than the imperial court council.
zh: 民事司法和国家法司法的结合，一般说来已经产生了这样的效果：现存帝国法院的事务量被扩大到它们无力办完的程度。
皇帝和帝国以及帝国最高法院都承认，帝国最高法院比帝国宫廷法院更加应付不了它的事务量。

en: No evil seems capable of easier remedy and [nothing] simpler [than] that, even if several separate courts should not be established, the number of judges of the existing courts be increased and thereby both the dispatch of business be immediately accelerated and also a division of the same court into several departments [be effected], and in this way several courts be established in point of fact.

But so simple a means is not possible to be carried out in Germany; it was indeed resolved and the number of assessors of the chamber court increased to 50, but the German Empire was unable to raise the salaries of these judges.
The number sank in the course of time to twelve and fewer, until it has finally come to twenty-five.
zh: 似乎没有哪一种弊病更容易得到补救，也没有〔什么〕比这更简单：即使不去设立几个分开的法院，也可以增加现有法院的法官人数，由此既直接加快事务的处理，又〔促成〕同一法院分成若干部门，这样一来，在事情本身的意义上就等于设立了好几个法院。
但这样一个简单的办法在德意志却不可能实行；它固然被议决了，帝国最高法院的陪席法官人数也增加到五十人，但德意志帝国却无力筹措这些法官的薪俸。
人数随着时间的推移降到十二人甚至更少，直到最后才到了二十五人。

en: The official calculations show that the number of legal suits made pending every year very much exceeds the number of those which it is possible to decide, if the relation of a single lawsuit does not, as otherwise happened, last several years, but yet sometimes several months, just as according to this many thousands of lawsuits necessarily and by counts actually undertaken lie undecided, and the solicitation of justice [Sollizitatur], even if its greatest abuses fall away and Jews no longer establish a trade in this article, is a necessary evil; for since it is impossible that all legal suits made pending be adjudged, it is necessary for the parties to give themselves every trouble that theirs receive the preference of a judicial decision.
zh: 官方的计算表明，每年被提起的讼案数目，远远超过可能判决的数目——如果一桩案子的审理不像往常那样拖上好几年，而毕竟有时候只拖上几个月的话；同样，照此必然如此，而且据实际作过的清点，也有好几千桩讼案搁在那里没有判决，于是催办诉讼〔Sollizitatur〕即使它最大的那些弊病消失、犹太人也不再拿这一项做买卖，仍然是一种必要的祸害；因为既然所有提起的讼案不可能都被判决，当事人就必然要费尽一切力气，好让自家的案子得到优先判决。

en: A thousand other collisions over the presentation of the assessors, the itio in partes, have often put the Imperial Chamber Court out of activity for several years, and without the Chamber Court's hesitating on purpose, from the principle of letting the great feel its power, they by themselves check the course of justice.
zh: 围绕陪审官之提名、围绕 itio in partes 的千百种别的冲突，常常使帝国枢密法院好几年无所作为；而枢密法院并不是有意出于要让大人物感觉到它的权力这一原则而拖延，这些冲突本身就在阻碍司法的进程。

en: It is natural that, since with the Imperial Court Council, whose members are appointed by the emperor, a mass of these evils falls away, also e.g., notwithstanding the right to it, no case of an itio in partes has yet occurred and many forms [are] suited to promote the right itself immediately, instead of engaging in delays of complete formalities, in more recent times justice is more and more sought at the Imperial Court Council.
zh: 很自然，既然在帝国宫廷参事院那里——它的成员由皇帝任命——这一大堆祸害都消失了，那么例如，尽管有那样做的权利，却还没有出现过一桩 itio in partes 的事例，而许多形式本来就是直接促进权利本身、而不是去纠缠于周全礼节的种种拖延的，〔所以〕在较近的时代，人们越来越到帝国宫廷参事院去寻求司法。

en: The need of an improvement of justice has always been too loud for one not to have been supposed to think of it; but the manner in which the last attempt of Joseph II to arrange an Imperial Chamber Court visitation, although one lawful according to imperial law, yet one omitted for two hundred years, turned out, and the grounds why people parted without having accomplished anything, are in general no other than those of the condition of imperial justice altogether, namely that the estates do indeed associate themselves for the administration of justice, but in this union want to give up nothing of their existence over against one another, which [rests] on separation and want of community, that [they] join together without yet wanting to have anything in common.
zh: 改善司法的需要从来就太响亮了，不可能不让人去考虑它；但是约瑟夫二世最后一次尝试举办一次帝国枢密法院巡察——这次巡察虽然合乎帝国法律，却已经中断了两百年——，其结果如何，以及人们为什么一事无成地散了伙，其理由总的说来不是别的，就是帝国司法状况本身的理由，也就是说：各等级固然为司法而联合起来，但在这个联合中，它们不肯放弃自己相对于彼此的、〔建立在〕分离和互不共同〔之上〕的那种存在，〔它们〕结合在一起，却又不愿有任何共同的东西。

en: In this way the pronouncing of judgment is already hindered in and for itself, without any regard to its execution.
But how it stands with the execution of these imperial-court decrees, if they should relate to constitutional law and to important objects of the same, is well known.
The more important matters belonging here belong anyway not to the imperial courts, but to the imperial diet.
Thereby they are played immediately out of the legal sphere into that of politics; for where the supreme state power speaks, there it does not make an application of the laws, but it gives a law.
zh: 这样一来，判决本身就已经受到阻碍，根本不必考虑它的执行。
但这些帝国法院的裁断，如果涉及国家法以及国家法的重要对象，它们的执行情况如何，是大家都知道的。
属于这一类的那些比较重要的事务，本来就不归帝国法院，而归帝国议会。
这样一来，它们就一下子从法律的领域被抛到政治的领域里去了；因为最高国家权力开口的地方，它不是在对法律作一种运用，而是在给出一条法律。

en: Besides, things of greater importance, the possession of lands etc., have also been withdrawn from this formality of the imperial diet, and through the electoral capitulation and other fundamental laws it is determined that about such objects it shall be decided not by the imperial courts and the supreme-judicial power, but by amicable settlement of the disputing estates among themselves, and if this does not go through by amicable settlement, then it happens necessarily through war.
zh: 此外，比较重要的事情，如对国土等等的占有，也被抽出了帝国议会这道手续；而且通过选举 capitulation〔Wahlkapitulation〕和别的根本法规定下来：这类对象不该由帝国法院和最高审判权力来裁断，而该由有争执的各等级彼此之间友好和解来裁断；如果友好和解行不通，那它就必然通过战争发生。

en: The Jülich-Berg succession affair was so little decided on the path of law that it rather occasioned a Thirty Years' War.
Thus in the Bavarian succession affair in more recent times it was not imperial courts but cannons and politics that spoke.
Also in matters which concern less powerful estates, it is not imperial justice that pronounces the deciding sentence.

It is well known that in the succession disputes of the Saxon houses over the lands of the extinct lines of Koburg-Eisenberg and -Römhild 206 Imperial Court Council conclusa were issued and the most important points were nevertheless decided by settlements.

Likewise it has been seen that in the Liège affair the Imperial Chamber Court not only pronounced the sentence and recognized execution and summoned several estates to it, but that these estates also really fulfilled this obligation.

But no sooner had the beginning been made than the most powerful estate among the executors was not content to be a mere executor of Imperial Chamber Court sentences, but went to work according to its own good intention and, when it did not go through that the matter be decided by a non-judicial path, also gave up the role of executor.
zh: 于利希—贝格继承事件，恰恰不是在法律的道路上得到裁断的，它反倒引起了一场三十年战争。
同样，在较近时代的巴伐利亚继承事件里，开口说话的不是帝国法院，而是大炮和政治。
即使在涉及不那么有权势的等级的事情上，作出决定性判词的也不是帝国司法。
大家都知道，在萨克森各家族因已绝嗣的科堡—艾森贝格和—勒姆希尔德两系之国土而起的继承争执中，发出过 206 件帝国宫廷参事院决议，可最重要的几点还是靠和解才决定了。
同样，人们也看到，在列日事件里，帝国枢密法院不仅作出了判决、认定了执行、并且为此传唤了好几个等级，而且这些等级也现实地履行了这项义务。
可是刚开了个头，执行者当中那个最有权势的等级就不满足于只当帝国枢密法院判词的一个执行者，而是照自己的一片好心干了起来，等到用非司法的途径来裁断行不通时，它连执行者的角色也一并丢开了。

en: If in such a delicate situation of a misunderstanding between prince and subject a mediation can be desirable, on the other hand, when judicial pronouncements have been issued, by the fact that in place of the execution a mediation is still to be put, the whole standpoint of the moment to which the matter has advanced, and through an apparently good effect for the moment, the essential principle of the constitution is displaced, or rather it becomes manifest on such occasions that it had long been displaced already beforehand.
zh: 在诸侯与臣民之间产生误会的这种棘手处境里，调解也许可以是值得盼望的；但反过来，一旦司法方面的判词已经作出，却还要在执行的位子上再放一个调解，那么事情已经达到的那个环节的整个立场，以及宪法那个本质的原则，就为着眼前一种表面上好的效果而被挪位了；或者不如说，在这种场合暴露出来的只是：它早就已经被挪位了。

en: On this point a distinction seems to have to be made.
It is too obvious that the relations of the powerful estates over against one another are decided by politics.
By contrast, however, the smaller estates seem to owe their existence simply and solely to the legal imperial union.

There is no imperial city that would hold itself capable of offering resistance to its neighbouring great fellow-estates, any more than an imperial knight believes himself able to assert his immediacy against a prince either through himself alone or through the union with the remaining corps of the imperial knighthood.

The matter speaks for itself, and it is superfluous to cite the fate of the imperial knighthood in Franconia; an attempt, and still less the success of an attempt, such as that of Franz von Sickingen to conquer an electorate, no longer belongs among the possible things of the present time, just as associations of imperial cities or abbots could no longer accomplish what they formerly were able to.
zh: 看起来，在这里必须作出一个区分。
太明显了，有权势的各等级彼此之间的关系是由政治来裁断的。
但与此相反，那些较小的等级似乎干脆就是靠法律上的帝国联合体才有其存在的。
没有一个帝国城市会认为自己有能力独自抵抗邻近的大同位等级，正如一个帝国骑士既不认为自己能靠自身、也不认为能靠与帝国骑士团其余部分的联合，来对一位诸侯保有自己的直属地位。
事情本身就说明了问题，用不着举法兰肯地区帝国骑士团的命运为例；像弗兰茨·冯·济金根那样去攻占一个选帝侯国的尝试，更不用说这种尝试的成功，已经不再属于当今可能的事情，正如帝国城市或修道院院长的联合也不再能做出它们从前所能做的事情。

en: If it is now not the power of the individual estates — nor even their power when they unite — that maintains them, then they seem to owe their existence as immediate and in a certain sense [in]dependent states to nothing other than the imperial union and the legal constitution that came about through the peace of the land.
But now the question is by what, then, this so-called legal relation, and with it the persistence of the knighthood, abbeys, imperial cities, counts etc., is still maintained.
Obviously not through its own power — for no state power is present — but likewise [through] politics.

If one does not regard politics immediately as the ground of the existence of the less powerful estates, that happens only because in the reasoning one stops at the imperial union, which constitutes a middle link, as at a ground, and forgets by what this imperial union is carried.
zh: 如果现在维系各等级的并不是单个等级的权力——也不是它们联合起来时的权力——，那么它们作为直接的、并且在某种意义上〔不〕依赖于人的国家而存在，看来就只该归功于帝国联合体和通过永久和平〔Landfrieden〕形成的法律宪制。
但现在的问题是：这种所谓的法律关系，以及随之而来的骑士团、修道院、帝国城市、伯爵等等的存续，究竟还靠什么来维持。
显然不是靠它自己的权力——因为根本没有什么国家权力在那里——，而同样〔是靠〕政治。
如果人们不把政治直接看作那些不那么有权势的等级之存在的根据，那只是因为人们在推理中停在帝国联合体这个中间环节上，把它当成了一个根据，而忘了这个帝国联合体是靠什么承载的。

en: States like Lucca, Genoa, etc. have preserved themselves for centuries without an imperial union, until they experienced the fate of Pisa, Siena, Arezzo, Verona, Bologna, Vicenza etc. etc. - in short, one could enumerate the whole geography of the cities, principalities, counties, etc. of Italy; the seemingly mightier republic [Venice], which had previously swallowed up so many independent cities, was put an end to by the arrival of an adjutant who delivered the mere command of the general of a foreign power.

These states, to which, while from the lottery of fate the several hundred Italian sovereign lands drew blanks, the few prizes of a somewhat prolonged independence had fallen, subsisted merely through the jealous policy of the larger states bordering them, with whose power they had in previous centuries been able to enter into a struggle, but, without external loss, had become quite disproportionately weak against them.

But in the equal share of the booty, in the equality of aggrandizement or diminution, the jealousy of policy likewise finds itself satisfied, and in the combinations of interests arising therefrom states like Venice, Poland, etc. are lost.
zh: 像卢卡、热那亚等国家，没有帝国联合体也维持了自己好几个世纪，直到它们也遭遇了比萨、锡耶纳、阿雷佐、维罗纳、博洛尼亚、维琴察等等等等的命运——总之，人们大可以把意大利的城市、诸侯国、伯爵领地等等的整个地理都数上一遍——而那个看来更强大的共和国[威尼斯]，先前吞掉了那么多独立的城市，却因为一个副官的到来就完了，这个副官送来的只不过是某个外国势力的一位将军的命令。
这些国家，在命运的抽奖中，意大利好几百个主权邦国大多抽到了空签，只有少数几个抽到了稍微延长了的独立这份彩头，它们仅仅是靠着与它们相邻的那些更大国家的猜忌政策才存在下来——在以往的世纪里它们还能和这些国家的力量较量一番，但后来虽然没有遭受外部的损失，却相对于它们变得完全不成比例地弱小。
但在战利品的同等份额里，在扩大或缩小的均等里，政策的猜忌同样得到了满足，而威尼斯、波兰等国家则在由此产生的种种利益组合中完了。

en: The transformation of the law of the fist into policy is not to be regarded as a transition from anarchy into a constitution.
The true principle has not changed, only its outward side.
In the condition before the public peace, the injured party or the one eager for conquest simply struck out.

In policy, on the other hand, one calculates before striking out, and for the sake of a small gain great interests are not put at stake, but where it seems possible to make it secure, it is not neglected.
zh: 拳头法向政策的转变，不能看作是从无政府状态向宪法的过渡。
真正的原则并没有改变，改变的只是它的外表。
在公共和平之前的状况里，受了伤害的人或者贪图征服的人，直接就动手打了。
相反，在政策里，动手之前先要计算，不会为了一点小收获就把重大的利益押上去，但只要这收获看来能够稳稳拿到，就不会放过。

en: Because the mass of the German states forms no power, the independence of their parts can be respected only as long as the advantage of other powers requires it and higher interests or even rights of compensation, etc., do not come into play.

As far as interest is concerned, France, for example, when its armies had occupied half of Germany, could just as well have abolished the constitutions of the lands on the right bank of the Rhine as it abolished the independent states and immediate estates in the Netherlands and in the lands of the left bank of the Rhine, which were afterwards ceded to France in the peace, and, even if this smashing of the independence of so many principalities, counties, bishoprics, abbeys, imperial cities, free lordships could not have lasted, would thereby have plunged these lands into still much greater misfortune, had not policy, namely the regard for Prussia and the feared complication of the peace, etc., and already the advantage which an order once established has for the collection of contributions, which according to the French official papers154) were levied in these lands to only a small extent, held it back.
zh: 因为德意志诸国的总体并不构成一种势力，所以它各部分的独立只能维持到这样的地步：只要其他势力的好处需要这样，而更高的利益或者还有要求补偿的权利等等还没有被牵涉进来。

就利益而言，比如法国，当它的军队占领了半个德意志的时候，它本可以像取消尼德兰以及莱茵河左岸各国中那些独立国家和直属帝国的等级——这些地方后来在和约中被割让给了法国——那样，也把莱茵河右岸各国的宪法取消掉，而且，即使这种对如此之多的诸侯国、伯爵领地、主教区、修道院、帝国城市、男爵领地的独立的摧毁无法长久维持，它本来也会借此把这些国家推入远远更大的不幸之中，要不是政策，也就是对普鲁士的顾忌、对和谈会变得更困难的担心等等，再加上一种一旦固定下来的秩序在征收赔款上已有的好处——按照法国官方公报154)，在这些国家里征收到的赔款是很少的——把它拦住了的话。

en: 155) This transition from the condition of open violence into the condition of calculated violence did not, of course, take place all at once; on the contrary, it happened through a lawful constitution.
After the public peace, one could indeed regard Germany as one state more readily than nowadays.
Through the feudal constitution state power was splintered into very many parts, but because of the multitude of the parts individual ones were not powerful enough to oppose themselves to the whole.

But as if fate had absolutely not destined Germany for such a condition, it soon overcame the weariness of lawlessness and the attempt at a firmer coherence through the public peace by means of the deeper interest of religion, which divided the peoples forever.
zh: 155) 从公开暴力的状态向算计过的暴力的状态的这一过渡，自然不是一下子完成的，相反，它是通过一种合乎权利的宪法发生的。
在公共和平之后，人们倒确实比今天更可以把德意志看作一个国家。
通过封建采邑制，国家权力被分裂成非常多的部分，但由于部分数量众多，单个部分并没有强大到足以与整体对抗。
但仿佛命运根本没有把德意志安排给这样一种状态似的，它很快又借着宗教那种更深的利益——这种利益使各民族永远彼此分裂——克服了对无法状态的厌倦，也克服了要通过公共和平达成更牢固联结的尝试。

en: Amid all the storms of the lawless condition of the times of feud, both with respect to the estates against one another and against the universal, a certain coherence of the whole subsisted.

If the fulfilment of obligations seemed to depend not only on the free will of the estates in general but on the wills of individuals, and the legal coherence seemed very weak, then on the other hand an inner coherence of minds prevailed.

Given the sameness of religion, and because the burgher estate, not yet risen, had not brought the great manifoldness into a whole, princes, counts and lords could regard one another as closer and more readily as a whole, and accordingly act as a whole.

There was no state power present that was opposed to the individuals and independent of them, as in modern states; the state power and the power and the free will of the individuals were one and the same.
But these individuals had rather the will to let themselves and their power subsist together in one state.
zh: 在私斗时代那种无法状态的一切风暴中，无论是就各等级相互之间来说，还是就它们与普遍者相对而言，整体都还保持着某种联结。
如果说义务的履行似乎不仅仅取决于各等级一般的自由意志，而是取决于各个个人的意志，而法律上的联结又显得十分微弱，那么与此相对，诸心灵之间却有一种内在的联结占着支配地位。
由于宗教相同，而且由于尚未上升起来的市民等级还没有把巨大的杂多带进整体之中，诸侯、伯爵和领主们便能把彼此看得更近，更容易看作一个整体，并因此作为一个整体来行动。
并不存在像现代国家里那样与各个个人相对立、并且独立于他们的国家权力；国家权力与各个个人的力量和自由意志是同一个东西。
但这些个人倒更愿意让自己和自己的权力在一个国家中共同维持下去。

en: But when, through the rise of the imperial cities, the burgher spirit, which cares only for a single thing without independence and without a view to the whole, began to become a power, this isolation of minds would have required a more universal, more positive bond, and when Germany, through the advance of culture and industry, had now been pushed to the crossroads of either resolving to obey a universal or tearing the connection apart completely, the original German character, of insisting on the free will of the individual and resisting subjection under a universal, carried off the victory and determined Germany's fate in accordance with its old nature.
zh: 但当随着帝国城市的兴起，那种只顾单个的东西、既没有独立性也不看整体的市民精神开始成为一种势力的时候，这种心灵上的孤立本来会要求一种更普遍、更确定的纽带；而当德意志由于教养和产业的推进终于被推到岔路口上，要么下决心去服从一个普遍者，要么干脆把联结彻底扯断的时候，德意志人那种原初的性格——坚持个人的自由意志、抗拒对一个普遍者的屈服——却取得了胜利，并按照它旧日的本性决定了德意志的命运。

en: In the course of time, great masses of states and the dominion of commerce and of industrial wealth had formed themselves; the unruliness of the German character could not directly promote the formation of independent states, the old free power of the nobility could not oppose itself to the masses that had arisen, and above all the burgher spirit, which was gaining standing and political significance, needed a kind of inner and outer legitimation.

The German character threw itself upon the innermost part of man, religion and conscience, from here consolidated the isolation, and the separation of the external as states appeared only as a consequence of this.
zh: 随着时间的推移，已经形成了大批的国家以及商业和手工业财富的统治；德意志性格的不羁不能直接去促成独立国家的形成，贵族旧日的自由力量也无法抵抗已经产生出来的这些集合体，尤其是那种正在赢得声望和政治分量的市民精神，还需要一种内在和外在的正当性。
德意志性格扑向人最内在的东西，即宗教和良心，并从这里出发把孤立固定下来，而外在的东西作为国家而彼此分离，看起来只是这件事的结果。

en: The original, never tamed character of the German nation determined the iron necessity of its fate.

Within the sphere given by this fate, politics, religion, need, virtue, violence, reason, cunning and all the powers that move the human race carry on, on the broad battlefield that is allowed them, their mighty, seemingly orderless play.

Each conducts itself as an absolutely free and independent power, unconscious that they are all tools in the hand of higher powers, of primordial fate and of time that conquers all, which laugh at that freedom and independence.
Even need, this mighty being, has not subdued the German character and its fate.

The universal misery of the religious wars and especially of the Thirty Years' War has rather developed its fate further and more strongly, and their results were a greater and more consolidated separation and isolation.
zh: 德意志民族那种原初的、从未被驯服的性格，决定了它命运的铁的必然性。
在这个命运所给定的范围之内，政策、宗教、困苦、美德、暴力、理性、狡计以及一切推动人类的力量，在允许它们占据的广阔战场上，进行着它们那强大的、看起来毫无秩序的游戏。
每一个都把自己当作一种绝对自由、独立的势力来行事，却没有意识到它们全都是更高的势力——原初的命运和战胜一切的时间——手中的工具，而这些势力正嘲笑那种自由和独立。
就连困苦这个强大的存在，也没有制服德意志性格和它的命运。
宗教战争、尤其是三十年战争的普遍苦难，反倒把它的命运发展得更远、更强，而它们的结果是一种更大、更稳固的分离和孤立。

en: Religion, instead of separating itself from the state through its own division, has rather carried this division into the state and contributed most to subverting the state, and has so woven itself into what is called constitution that it is a condition of state rights.
zh: 宗教不是通过它自身的分裂把自己从国家中分离出去，反倒是把这种分裂带进了国家，并且最有力地促成了国家的瓦解，还这样把自己织进了所谓宪法的东西里，以致它成了国家权利的条件。

en: Already in the particular states of which Germany consists, even civil rights are tied to it.
In this intolerance [both] religions have an equal share, and neither has anything to reproach the other with.
The Austrian and Brandenburg princes, in defiance of the intolerance laid down by imperial law, esteemed religious freedom of conscience higher than the barbarism of rights.
zh: 在构成德意志的那些个别邦里，连市民权利都已经和它捆在一起了。
在这种不宽容上，[两个]宗教占有同等的份额，哪一个都没有什么可以责备另一个的。
奥地利和勃兰登堡的君主们不顾帝国法律规定的这种不宽容，把宗教上的良心自由看得比权利的野蛮更高。

en: The disorder caused by the separation of religion was especially strong in Germany, because the bond of the state was looser in no country than in this one, and the ruling religion had to be all the more embittered against those who separated themselves, because with religion not only the innermost bond of human beings was torn apart, but because thereby, so to speak, almost the only bond was torn apart, whereas in other states a multitude of connections still remained in their firmness.

Because already the community of religion is a deeper community, that of physical needs, of property, of acquisition on the other hand a lower one, and the demand for separation is in itself more unnatural than the demand that an existing union remain, the Catholic church showed itself more fanatical, because its demand went in general to union and to the holiest thing of this union, and it wanted to hear at most of grace and toleration, nothing of right, that is, of the fixing of the separation, upon which Protestantism insisted.
Both parties finally came together on this: to exclude each other civilly and to surround and secure this exclusion with all the pedantry of right.
zh: 宗教分裂所造成的混乱在德意志格外厉害，因为国家的纽带在任何国家里都不如在这个国家里这样松散，而占统治地位的宗教也就必然对分离出去的人更为恼怒，因为随着宗教被撕断的不只是人最内在的纽带，而是这样一来几乎唯一的纽带都被撕断了，相反在别的国家里还有许多连接依然牢固如故。
因为宗教的共同体本就是一种更深的共同体，而肉体需要、财产、营生的共同体则是一种较低的共同体，又因为分离的要求本身比现有的结合应当保持的要求更不合自然，所以天主教会显得更为狂热，因为它的要求总的来说指向结合，而且指向这种结合中最神圣的东西，它顶多只愿意听恩典和容忍，绝不愿听权利，也就是不愿听对分离的固定，而新教恰恰坚持这一点。
双方最后一致同意：在市民意义上互相排斥，并且用权利的全部迂执把这种排斥包围起来、固定下来。

en: The appearance is the same, that in Catholic countries civil rights are denied to the Protestants and in Protestant ones to the Catholics.
Yet the ground seems different.

The Catholics had the position of oppressors, the Protestants that of the oppressed: the Catholics [had] denied the Protestants as criminals the free exercise of religion in their midst; for the Protestants, where their church was dominant, this ground falls away as does the anxiety of being oppressed.

The ground of Protestant intolerance could only be either the right of retaliation for the hatred and intolerance of the Catholics - which would have been too unchristian a motive - or a mistrust of the power and truth of one's own faith and the fear of easy seduction by the splendor of Catholic worship and the zeal of its adherents, etc.
zh: 现象是同一个：在天主教国家里新教徒被剥夺市民权利，在新教国家里天主教徒被剥夺市民权利。
不过根据似乎不同。
天主教徒处于压迫者的地位，新教徒处于被压迫者的地位：天主教徒[曾]把新教徒当作罪犯，[拒绝]他们在自己中间自由举行宗教活动；对新教徒来说，在他们的教会占统治地位的地方，这个根据就不成立了，被压迫的担忧也不成立了。
新教不宽容的根据只可能是这样：要么是对天主教徒的仇恨和不宽容施以报复的权利——这会是一个太不合基督教的动机——要么是对自己信仰的力量和真理的不信任，以及害怕人们轻易就被天主教的礼拜的排场和它信徒的热忱所引诱，等等。

en: Especially in the previous century this eternal fear, that the Protestant faith might be outwitted and stolen upon, this faith, watchman-of-Zion-like, in its own powerlessness and fear of the cunning of the enemy, was dominant and the occasion for entrenching the grace of God behind unspeakable security measures and bulwarks of rights.
zh: 尤其在上一世纪，这种永恒的对新教信仰会被智取而悄悄潜入的恐惧，这种像锡安守望者一样对自己无力的笃信和对敌人狡计的恐惧，是占统治地位的，也是人们用说不尽的保险措施和权利的壁垒把上帝那里的恩典围护起来的起因。

en: This relation of right has been asserted with the greatest embitterment, when it was presented by individuals of the opposing party as a matter of grace; and indeed grace is on the one hand lower than right, for right is determinate and what is rightful has been made involuntary for both parties, and grace is for right only arbitrariness.
Through this holding fast to pure, bare right, however, the higher sense of grace has also been obscured, so that for a long time no party raised itself above right and let grace go before right.
What Frederick II and Joseph did, the former against the Catholics, the latter against the Protestants, was grace against the rights of the Peace of Prague and the Peace of Westphalia.

It coincides with higher natural rights of freedom of conscience and of the independence of civil rights from faith, but these higher rights are in the Religious Peace and the Peace of Westphalia not only not recognized but excluded, and their exclusion guaranteed in the most solemn manner by Protestants as well as Catholics, and from this standpoint there is so little to insist upon these guaranteed rights that the grace which is spurned is infinitely higher.
zh: 这种权利关系曾被以最大的恼怒坚持，当对方阵营的个别人把它表象为一件恩典的事情时；而恩典确实一方面比权利低，因为权利是确定了的，而合乎权利的东西对双方都成了不由己的，恩典对权利来说只是任意。
但通过这种对纯粹、单纯的权利的坚持，恩典的更高意义也被弄暗了，以致很长时间没有哪一方超越权利，让恩典先于权利而行。
腓特烈二世和约瑟夫所做的事，前者针对天主教徒，后者针对新教徒，是违背布拉格和约与《威斯特伐利亚和约》的权利的恩典。
它与良心自由和市民权利独立于信仰这些更高的自然权利相合，但这些更高的权利在宗教和约与《威斯特伐利亚和约》里不仅没有被承认，反而被排除，而且它们的被排除还由新教徒和天主教徒同样以最郑重的方式加以保证，从这个立场出发，对这些被保证的权利根本没有什么可倚仗的，以致那被鄙弃的恩典要无限地更高。

en: Religion is an even more important determining ground of the relation of the individual parts of Germany to the whole; it has probably contributed most to tearing apart the union of the state and to making this tearing apart lawful.

The times in which religion split were too unskilled to separate the church from the state and, despite the separation of faiths, to preserve the latter, and the princes could find no better ally for withdrawing themselves from the overlordship of the empire than the conscience of their subjects.
zh: 宗教是德意志各个别部分对整体的关系的一个更重要的规定根据；它大概最有力地促成了国家结合的撕断，并且使这种撕断成了合法的。
宗教发生分裂的那些时代太笨拙，既不能把教会与国家分开，又不能不顾信仰的分裂而把国家保住，而君主们要想摆脱帝国的最高统治权，再找不到比他们臣民的良心更好的盟友了。

en: By virtue of the imperial laws gradually formed thereby, the religion of every country, of every imperial city is determined by law, the one declared purely Catholic, another purely Protestant, a third parity.
How would it be, then, if a country violated the Peace of Westphalia so greatly as to pass from one purity into another purity or from parity into purity?
zh: 凭着由此逐渐形成的帝国法律，每个邦、每个帝国城市的宗教都由法律确定了，这一个被宣布为纯粹天主教的，那一个被宣布为纯粹新教的，第三个被宣布为两教并存的。
那么，要是一个邦如此严重地违反《威斯特伐利亚和约》，从一种纯粹状态转入另一种纯粹状态，或者从两教并存转入纯粹状态，又当如何呢？

en: Just as fixed is the religion of the votes of the imperial diet, of the imperial chamber court, of the imperial court council, of the individual offices and posts, etc.; among these state relations determined according to religion the most important is the so famous itio in partes, the right of the one or the other religious part not to submit itself to the majority of votes.
If this right were restricted to religious matters, the justice and necessity of this right would be self-evident.
The separation would be immediately harmless for the state, because it would concern only objects that fundamentally do not concern it.

But by virtue of the itio in partes the separation of the minority from the majority is legitimized in every state affair that has nothing at all to do with religion; about war and peace, the raising of an imperial army, taxes, in short about all the little that earlier times had still left over as the shadow of a whole, the majority of votes is by law not decisive, but even without any effectiveness of policy the minority, which forms a religious party, can check the activity of the state.
zh: 同样被固定的还有帝国议会、帝国最高法院、帝国宫廷法院的票数、各个官职和职位等的宗教；在这些按宗教确定的国家关系里，最重要的就是那个如此著名的 itio in partes，即这一方或那一方宗教派别有不服从多数票的权利。
如果这项权利被限制在宗教事务上，那么这项权利的正当性和必要性就不言而喻了。
这种分离对国家就会直接无害，因为它只涉及根本上与国家无关的对象。
但凭着 itio in partes，少数派对多数派的分裂在每一件与宗教毫无关系的国家事务上都被合法化了；关于战争与和平、征召帝国军队、赋税，简言之关于较早的时代还留下来当作一个整体的影子的那一点点事情，多数票在法律上并不是决定性的，而且即使政治完全不起作用，组成一个宗教派别的少数派也能使国家的活动受阻。

en: It is going too far when one, as some do, places this right in parallel with the right of insurrection hallowed in some of the many kinds of French constitutions that have been made within a decade.

For one must regard Germany as an already dissolved state and its parts, which do not submit themselves to a majority of the whole, as independent states existing in themselves, whose separation, if they cannot reach a common conclusion, does not inevitably have as its consequence the dissolution of all social bonds and not always internal wars.
zh: 如果有人像某些人那样，把这项权利与近十年来制定的各式各样的法国宪法中有些宪法所尊为神圣的起义权相提并论，那就走得太远了。
因为必须把德意志看作一个已经瓦解的国家，把它的那些不服从整体多数的部分看作独立的、自在存在的国家，它们的分裂如果不能达成一个共同的结论，并不必然导致一切社会纽带的解体，也不总是导致内战。

en: But in that religion has completely torn the state apart, it has at the same time, in a wonderful way, given the presentiment of some principles on which a state can rest.

In that its division tore men apart in their innermost being, and yet a connection was still to remain, it must connect itself outwardly over external things, waging war, etc., - a connection that is the principle of modern states.

Precisely by the fact that the most important parts of state right were woven into the religious division, two religions have been woven into the state, and thereby all political rights have been made dependent on two, or actually three, religions; [indeed] the principle of the independence of the state from the church, and of the possibility of a state despite the diversity of religions, has [thus] been contravened, but in fact [by this], that different religions exist and Germany is to be a state, it [this principle] has been recognized.
zh: 但是，宗教既然把国家完全撕碎了，它同时也以一种奇妙的方式让人预感到了一些原则，一个国家是可以建立在这些原则之上的。
它的分裂把人在最内在的本质中撕开，却又应当还留下一种联结，于是它就必须在一些外在的事情上、在打仗等等上面从外部联结起来，——这样一种联结，就是现代国家的原则。
恰恰由于国家法最重要的那些部分被织进了宗教的分裂，就有两个宗教被织进了国家，从而一切政治权利都被弄得取决于两个、其实是三个宗教；〔固然〕这样一来，国家独立于教会这条原则、以及一个国家不顾宗教差别而可能成立这一点，都遭到了违背，但实际上〔正因如此〕，由于存在着不同的宗教，而德意志又应当是一个国家，这条原则还是得到了承认。

en: More important is another separation, which has likewise been brought about by religion and lies still closer to the possibility of the state.

Originally, namely, the votes in the general deliberations and resolutions rested on the full personality of the princes; they had votes only when they appeared in person, and the prince of several, otherwise separate lands had only one vote.
Their person and their land, the personality and the quality of representing a land, did not appear separated.
Through the religious division this distinction came to the fore.

To which side should a vote hold, when the prince and his land were of different religions and when a vote had once been counted, according to the fundamental laws of the empire, to one religious party?
zh: 更重要的是另一种分离，它同样是由宗教带来的，而且离国家的可能性更近。
因为当初在一般的商议和决议中，票是建立在诸侯的完整人格之上的；他们只有亲自到场才有票，而一个统治着几个本来彼此分离的地方的诸侯也只有一票。
他们的人身和他们的地方、人格和代表一个地方的身份，并不显得是分开的。
通过宗教的分裂，这个区别才显露出来。
当一个诸侯和他的地方属于不同的宗教，而一票又曾经按照帝国根本法被算作某一个宗教党派的时候，这一票该站到哪一边去呢？

en: As state power he should be on neither side at all, but the times had not ripened for this.
On this too, at first, no such reflection was made.

The prince of the Protestant Palatinate-Neuburg, who became Catholic in the 17th century, was counted at the imperial diet as well as in the imperial courts among the Catholic votes, whereas the vote of the Elector of Saxony, who at the end of that very same century156) changed religion, remained Protestant, as was also the case with the religious changes of the princes of Hessen [and] of Württemberg that occurred later.
zh: 作为国家权力，他本来不该站在任何一边，但时代还没有发展到这一步。
对这一点，起初也没有作这样的反思。
新教方面普法尔茨-诺伊堡的诸侯在17世纪成了天主教徒，他在帝国议会以及在帝国法院里都被算进天主教的票里；相反，萨克森选侯的票却仍然是新教的——这位选侯在同一世纪将尽时156)改变了宗教，正如后来黑森〔和〕符腾堡的诸侯们改变宗教时也是这种情况一样。

en: Although even before, seat and vote at the imperial diet belonged only to princes who had land and people to govern, so that a land seemed inseparable from the concept of an estate at the imperial diet, yet this distinction between the personality of the prince and his representing a land became more visible also with regard to the general German state, and all the more easily, when within the land this separation of the person of the prince and his subjects had already been constituted through provincial estates.

The Palatinate, which had no provincial estates, went over to the Catholic side without resistance, and the struggle of the Palatines with their Catholic princes over religious grievances continued down to the most recent times, whereas in Hessen and in Württemberg the separation had already become legal through provincial estates, and the religion of the land was also asserted with regard to its relation to the German Empire and [was] placed before the personality of the prince, and he thus appears at the imperial diet not as an individual but as a representative.
zh: 虽然在此以前，也只有那些有地方和人民要治理的诸侯才在帝国议会里拥有席位和票，所以一个地方看来同帝国议会中一个等级的概念不可分离，但诸侯的人格与他代表一个地方这重身份之间的这个区别，在考虑到整个德意志国家时也变得更明显，而且如果在一个地方内部，诸侯本人和他的臣民之间的这种分离已经通过地方等级确立起来，这个区别就更加容易显露。
普法尔茨没有地方等级，就毫无抵抗地转到了天主教那一边，而普法尔茨人由于宗教上的申诉同他们的天主教诸侯进行的斗争一直持续到最近的时代；相反，在黑森和符腾堡，这种分离通过地方等级已经合法化了，地方自己的宗教也就同德意志帝国的关系而言得到主张，并被置于诸侯的人格之前，于是这诸侯在帝国议会里就不是作为个人、而是作为代表出现。

en: The attention to this distinction, which religion has occasioned, has now extended to other differences, and lands that have come under one prince have obtained separate votes for the prince, and in this too it is no longer, as formerly, when the regent of several principalities likewise had only one vote, or several princes, among whom one principality was divided, likewise each had a vote for himself, the unity of the individual, thus not the personality but his quality of being a representative, that has been made the principle.
zh: 对这种由宗教引起的区别的注意，如今扩展到了别的差异上去，而那些归到一个诸侯之下的地方，也为该诸侯取得了单独的票；在这方面，被当作原则的也已经不再像从前那样是那个个人的统一、也就是不再是人格，而是他作为代表的身份——从前，一个统治着几个侯国的君主也同样只有一票，或者当几个诸侯分有一个侯国时，每个诸侯也各自有一票。

en: But as the nourishment of a healthy body, used by a sick body, would corrupt it still more, so this true and genuine principle, that the land gives force and right to the vote, [when] brought into the condition of the German Empire, has all the more contributed to its dissolution.
zh: 但是，就像一个健康身体的养料被一个生病的身体用了反而会更厉害地败坏它，这个真实而地道的原则——即地方赋予票以力量和权利——一旦被放进德意志帝国的状况之中，就更加促成了它的解体。
